description: Notebook rename from the UI (user_instruction change 3). Let the user change a notebook's name both DURING creation and AFTER, via an edit button in the interface. REUSE the existing useRenameNotebook mutation in src/features/notebook/api.ts (do NOT add a migration or new backend). Add the edit affordance in BOTH notebook surfaces: the full page (src/features/notebook/NotebookPage.tsx) and the floating overlay (src/features/notebook/NotebookOverlay.tsx). Match existing UI primitives (Button/Input in src/components/ui).
steps: In src/features/notebook/NotebookPage.tsx: import useRenameNotebook from ./api and instantiate it with userId. Next to each notebook name button in the 'Cadernos' list, add a pencil/'Editar' edit button. Clicking it switches that notebook's name into an inline editable state (use the shared Input component) with Save and Cancel actions; Save calls renameNotebook.mutateAsync({ id, title }) and on success the list refetches (the hook already invalidates notebookKeys.list). Trim empty -> fallback handled by the hook. Keep the existing select/delete behavior intact. Also allow setting the name at creation: when 'Novo caderno' is created, immediately put it into the inline-edit state (or prompt) so the user can name it right away.

In src/features/notebook/NotebookOverlay.tsx: import and use useRenameNotebook(userId). Add an edit (pencil) button in the notebook picker row (next to the <select> and the create/delete buttons) that, when the current notebook is selected, switches the title to an inline Input with Save/Cancel wired to renameNotebook. On create of a new notebook, enter the inline-edit state so the name can be set at creation. Preserve the existing drag/resize, page tabs, and editor behavior. Keep styling consistent with .nb-overlay* classes / existing Button component (do not introduce Tailwind).

Ensure new state (editing id, draft title) is local component state; invalidate/refetch via the existing mutation onSuccess (no new query keys). Keep accessibility: the edit button needs an aria-label (e.g. `Renomear caderno ${title}`), and the inline input needs an aria-label/label.
Confirm no edits are made to src/types/db.ts, src/types/database.ts, or supabase/migrations.
acceptance_criteria: NotebookPage shows an edit button per notebook that opens an inline Input to rename, persisting via useRenameNotebook and refreshing the list on success.
NotebookOverlay shows an edit button for the selected notebook that renames it inline via the same hook.
A newly created notebook can be named immediately (name editable at creation time) in at least the page surface, via the same inline-edit flow.
No backend/schema/type changes; only src/features/notebook/*.tsx (and possibly a reused import) are touched. No new eslint/TS warnings.
verification: npm run lint reports no new warnings
git diff --name-only shows no changes under supabase/ or src/types/
findings: Implemented notebook rename UI in both surfaces, reusing the existing useRenameNotebook(userId) mutation (no backend/schema/type changes). Files touched: src/features/notebook/NotebookPage.tsx and src/features/notebook/NotebookOverlay.tsx. NotebookPage: added local editingNotebookId + draftTitle state; each notebook row now has a pencil (✏️) edit button with aria-label `Renomear caderno ${title}` that swaps the name button for a shared Input (aria-labelled) with Save(✔)/Cancel(✕); Enter saves, Escape cancels; Save calls renameNotebook.mutateAsync({ id, title }). handleCreateNotebook now enters inline-edit on the new notebook so it can be named at creation. NotebookOverlay: same local state; picker row shows a pencil edit button for the selected notebook that swaps the <select> for an inline input with Save/Cancel wired to the same hook; create also enters inline-edit. Drag/resize/page-tabs/editor preserved; input onPointerDown stops propagation so typing in the overlay body does not interfere. Verification: npm run typecheck exit 0; npm run lint exit 0 with 5 pre-existing warnings and NO new ones (the two NotebookPage exhaustive-deps warnings are the known pre-existing ones, just at shifted line numbers 72/82); npm run test 208/208 passed; npm run build exit 0. git diff --name-only confirms no changes under supabase/ or src/types/. This change is UI wiring verified via typecheck/lint/test/build (no new pure helper to unit-test).
